new_scholarship.official_source: European University Institute (EUI) — Max Weber Programme for Postdoctoral Studies
new_scholarship.description: The Max Weber Programme is the postdoctoral programme of the European University Institute, an intergovernmental research institute of the European Union based at Badia Fiesolana near Florence. It awards 1- and 2-year fellowships of EUR 2,500 per month to researchers within five years of completing their PhD, from any nationality. A cohort typically comprises around 65 Fellows distributed across the EUI academic units, and the annual acceptance rate is stated to be under 2%. The current call is for a 1 September 2027 start with an application deadline of 16 October 2026.

new_scholarship.name: EASL Mobility / Research Fellowship Programme
new_scholarship.program_type: Professional association research and mobility fellowship
new_scholarship.official_source: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)
new_scholarship.description: EASL runs an annual fellowship programme with two categories, Mobility Fellowships and Research Fellowships, each lasting six months and worth up to EUR 25,000. Mobility Fellowships fund temporary secondments of researchers to a host institute in Europe, while Research Fellowships fund focused projects carried out at the applicant's own institution. Three awards are made per round, applicants must be EASL members, and the budget must also cover attending a future EASL Congress to present results. The 2026 call ran from 15 July to 1 September 2026 and is closed; the programme states a fixed annual application period of 15 July to 1 September.

new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Early- or mid-career professionals affiliated with a recognised clinical or scientific institution or university in Europe, must be EASL members, and the project must focus on liver disease. Mobility fellowships additionally require a host institute in Europe and a letter confirming it can host the applicant.

Weighting published by EASL: scientific/clinical merit 35%, applicant's motivation 20%, applicant's potential 15%, relevance to hepatology 15%, host institution and environment 15%. Final decisions also consider diversity, equity and potential long-term impact.

new_scholarship.program_type: Foundation-funded doctoral scholarship for study and research in Germany
new_scholarship.official_source: Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes (German Academic Scholarship Foundation)
new_scholarship.description: The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is Germany's largest scholarship foundation and funds around 350 new doctoral students each year with a monthly stipend of EUR 1,650 for three years. Since 2024 it has replaced regional application rounds with four fixed two-week calls a year, each opening about eight months before the selection meeting. Applications are accepted only by post and must be complete. The current call runs from 1 to 14 October 2026, with the selection meeting in May 2027 and the earliest possible scholarship start on 1 July 2027.
new_scholarship.duration: Three years, extendable by up to six months on application, and by up to 12 months on childbirth
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Doctoral students who are German citizens or who obtained their higher education entrance qualification in Germany and are pursuing a doctorate at a German university; the previous degree must normally have been completed within the last four years and three months, and applicants are expected to be among the top 15% of their cohort.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Two selection phases. Applicants are assessed on the academic standard of the previous degree, individual organisation of studies, commitment to social causes and the scientific quality of the doctoral project, which is reviewed in the second phase by two academically qualified reviewers. Scholars are not given bonus points, but statistically former scholarship holders are more likely to be funded. Involvement in security-relevant research requires a signed declaration before the procedure can proceed.

new_scholarship.notes: Funding can only begin once doctoral study has started full-time. Part-time work is permitted up to 0.25 of a full-time position in research and teaching, or a maximum of five hours a week elsewhere. A doctoral scholarship from another institution may not be held at the same time, and holders must report any other scholarship offered to them. The foundation offers no institutional insurance cover, does not pay thesis printing costs, and applicants pay their own travel costs to the second-stage interview.

application_readiness_checklist: Secure EAN RRFS or Full membership at least three weeks before the window closes
Choose the track: Research Training (6 to 12 months, career-stage output required) or Research Experience (3 to 6 months)
Get a written host acceptance from the chair of the host department with the mentor's CV and bibliography
Draft the full project description with background, aims, methods, timetable and references
Keep every original document, as fresh copies may be requested
common_rejection_risks: Applying outside the 1 June to 31 August window
Sending documents by e-mail or hand, which EAN does not consider
More than two years of clinical training missing for an RRFS applicant, or the five-year window since the latest neurology degree having expired for a Full member
A weak feasibility or methods section, which EAN flags as among the heaviest weighted scores
Missing host acceptance letter or mentor CV
estimated_uncovered_costs: Salary or income lost during the fellowship, which EAN does not fund
Visa, insurance, relocation and family costs

alerts.message: The 2027 call closed on 31 August 2026; the next window is expected to open on 1 June 2027, so prepare documents in advance.
Successful fellowships can be applied from 1 September 2026 where the stay started earlier, so an early start may still be claimable in the next round.
Travel money is only reimbursed after the fellowship ends, so you must fund the trip up front.

submission_workflow: Confirm EAN RRFS or Full membership and apply at least three weeks before the deadline if needed
Decide between the Research Training and Research Experience tracks
Agree the project and dates with a host department outside your country and obtain the host acceptance letter
Complete the EAN CV form, project description and both recommendations
Submit everything through the EAN online application form during the 1 June to 31 August window
Await the outcome by the end of November and file the final report and evaluation forms for travel reimbursement
